about: Every key of every JSON document ai-usage-tui prints, and every value of every closed vocabulary. Printed by `ai-usage-tui --schema`. Within a schema_version keys are only added. Read `ai-usage-tui --agent-guide` for how to use these documents.
rules: null means unknown or not recorded. It never means 0. A cost of null is not free; a percentage of null is not 0%.
cost is dollars actually billed per token. When cost_is_floor is true (or unpriced_requests > 0) it leaves requests out and is a minimum, not a total.
quota_requests were billed against a subscription plan: real cost with no per-request dollar figure. They are never in cost.
api_equivalent_cost is what subscription requests would have cost at API list rates. It was never charged. It is not spend and not savings.
Percentages are on the 0..100 scale. Timestamps are unix seconds. Token counts are disjoint: input excludes cache, output excludes reasoning.

category.LOCAL: Ran on a local endpoint. Genuinely zero cost.
category.FREE: A model the pricing table marks free, or whose id ends in a provider's documented free suffix (-free, :free) and that the table lists no rate for. Genuinely zero cost.
category.PAID: A provider that bills per token, including aggregators and clouds. Whether a rate is known is cost_status.
category.CLOUD: Hosted or cloud-routed usage without an authoritative cost.
category.UNKNOWN: Provider not recognised as billing per token.

cost_status.calculated: The source tool calculated it from its own rates.
cost_status.estimated: ai-usage-tui estimated it from its pricing table.
cost_status.free: Explicitly free. Cost is a real 0.
cost_status.local: Local model. Cost is a real 0.
cost_status.quota: Billed against a subscription plan. Real cost, no per-request figure: cost is null.
cost_status.unavailable: Should carry a price and has none: no rate is known for the model, or the record was missing a token count and was not priced from the rest. cost is null.

billing.subscription: Paid through a plan; rows become cost_status quota.

cost_basis.exact: Every contributing task carried a price. cost_per_success is a real figure.
cost_basis.floor: Some spend was priced and some was not. cost_per_success is null: a minimum is not printed as though it were the figure. cost holds the priced part.
cost_basis.plus_quota: Some tasks were priced, the rest billed against a plan. cost_per_success is null.
cost_basis.quota: Every task was billed against a plan; there is no dollar figure. cost_per_success is null.
cost_basis.unpriced: Nothing was priced and something should have been. cost_per_success is null.
cost_basis.free: Every task was free or local. cost_per_success is a real 0.
cost_basis.no_successes: No task passed, so there is no denominator. cost_per_success is null: unknown, not zero.

budget_level.WARN: At or past warn (default 75% of limit).
budget_level.CRITICAL: At or past critical (default 90% of limit).

budget_period.monthly: Since the first of the local calendar month.

bucket.meaning: One rollup. Every list in --summary-json is made of these.

tokens.meaning: Sum of the five token counts below.

output_tokens.meaning: Completion tokens, excluding reasoning where the source splits it.

reasoning_tokens.meaning: Reasoning tokens, where the source reports them separately. Claude Code does not.

cost.meaning: Dollars over priced requests. null when the bucket holds paid work and none of it could be priced (all quota or unpriced). 0 only when everything is free, local, or the bucket is empty.

cost_is_floor.meaning: true when cost leaves unpriced requests out.

priced_requests.meaning: Requests that carry a dollar cost.

unpriced_requests.meaning: Requests that should carry a price and do not.

quota_requests.meaning: Requests billed against a subscription plan.

api_equivalent_cost.meaning: List-rate value of the quota requests. Never charged.

metrics.meaning: Derived figures. Facts, not verdicts; null when nothing recorded supports one.

share_of_tokens_pct.meaning: This bucket's tokens as a share of the document's totals.

cache_hit_pct.meaning: cache_read / (input + cache_read + cache_write). null when no cache tokens were recorded at all: several sources never report them, so that is not a 0% hit rate.

output_pct.meaning: output_tokens as a share of tokens.

reasoning_pct.meaning: reasoning_tokens as a share of tokens. null when none were recorded.

cost_per_request.meaning: cost / priced_requests. Unpriced and quota requests are not averaged in as free.

bucket_brief.meaning: The bucket without its five-way token split, used by day and session rows. Same keys at the same paths. Drill down with --session or --days for the split.

stale.meaning: Too old to trust as current.

resets_in_secs.meaning: Seconds until then; negative if already past.

escalations.meaning: Sessions that moved to a pricier model, derived from usage (not from recorded routing events).

sessions_examined.meaning: Sessions with enough requests to show a change.

sessions_escalated.meaning: Of those, how many moved to a pricier model.

escalation_rate.meaning: Percent. null when no session could be examined.

unclassified_changes.meaning: Model changes that could not be ordered because a rate was missing.

to.meaning: The pricier model it moved to, by the pricing table's input rate. Never the cheaper one: a move down is not listed.

from_input_rate.meaning: List price of `from`, dollars per million input tokens.

to_input_rate.meaning: List price of `to`. Higher than from_input_rate: that is what makes it an escalation.

cost_after.meaning: Dollars spent on the pricier model afterwards. A floor when unpriced_after or quota_after is non-zero.

unpriced_after.meaning: Requests after the move with no price.

quota_after.meaning: Requests after the move billed against a plan.

provenance.meaning: Where the dollar figures came from.

reported_share.meaning: Percent of billable dollars a provider reported rather than this tool worked out. null with no billable dollars.

billable_cost.meaning: Dollars across reported, calculated and estimated.

by_cost_status.meaning: One entry per cost_status, always all seven.

budget.meaning: One configured budget and where spend stands against it.

period.meaning: The budget's own period; range flags do not apply.

spend.meaning: Priced dollars in the period. A floor when unpriced_requests > 0. Quota work is never in it.

quota_requests.meaning: In-scope requests billed against a plan.

routing_withheld.meaning: Test runs --claude-code-hook saw and did not record: the command line's exit status was not the test runner's own (it was piped, chained or substituted) and the output held no summary line the tool can read. A count only; no command line or output is stored. Read it beside events: two events and 800 withheld is a coverage gap, two events and none is a quiet machine.

by_reason.meaning: The same runs by reason, most first.

reason.meaning: pipe, sequence, or_after, after_or, background, substitution or and_chain. New labels may be added.

meaning.meaning: The reason in words. null for a label written by a newer build.

routing_aggregate.meaning: Recorded routing events (test runs journaled by --claude-code-hook or --record-routing) grouped by agent, model and provider.

agent.meaning: Harness or role that ran the task.

cost.meaning: Dollars over priced tasks; null when none was priced.

unpriced_tasks.meaning: Tasks that should have one and do not.

cost_per_success.meaning: Dollars per task that passed its tests. A figure only when cost_basis is exact or free; null otherwise, and cost_basis says why.

success_rate.meaning: Percent of tasks with a test result that passed. null when none recorded one.

retries.meaning: Sum; null when no task reported a count.

escalations.meaning: Sum; null when no task reported a count.

review_defects.meaning: Sum; null when no task reported a count.

retries_observed.meaning: Tasks that reported a retry count: the denominator of retry_rate.

retry_rate.meaning: Percent of observed tasks that retried at least once.

escalation_rate.meaning: Percent of observed tasks that escalated.

defect_rate.meaning: Percent of observed tasks with a review defect.

--summary-json.meaning: The compact aggregated document. Start here. Honours --today/--week/--month/--days N/--all (default: 7 days), --provider, --model, --project, --session, --top N.

label.meaning: TODAY, 7 DAYS, 30 DAYS, N DAYS or ALL TIME.

since.meaning: Start of the range; null for all history.

filters.meaning: Filters applied; null when not given.

sources.meaning: Every data source, found or not. Not narrowed by range or filters.

id.meaning: opencode, claude_code, codex, copilot, gemini, journal, zen_pricing.

present.meaning: Whether anything was there to read.

status.meaning: One-line status, including data that was skipped, records missing a token count (kept, unpriced) and records with no timestamp (in no range but --all).

detail.meaning: How billing was decided for this source, or why it is off.

build.meaning: The binary that wrote this document. What --doctor prints under THIS BUILD.

install_channel.meaning: How the running binary was installed, judged from where it is: cargo, Homebrew, Scoop, a system package, the install script, or an unrecognised location.

upgrade_command.meaning: The command that upgrades an install of that kind. null when the location is not recognised: run none, and point at the releases page.

update.meaning: The last cached answer of the opt-in update check. null means nothing has ever asked, not that this build is current. Writing this document never checks.

latest.meaning: The newest release tag, as GitHub reported it.

checked_at.meaning: Unix seconds when it was asked. An old answer can only understate.

newer.meaning: Whether latest is newer than version.

currency.meaning: USD. Every cost and rate in every document is US dollars at list price; nothing is converted.

models_priced.meaning: Model names the table can price.

community_table_date.meaning: YYYY-MM-DD the bundled community (LiteLLM) rates were snapshotted. Estimated costs rest on rates as of this date.

curated_table_date.meaning: YYYY-MM-DD the bundled curated (Zen and hand-checked) rates were updated. A fresh --refresh-pricing cache supersedes it.

warnings.meaning: Problems loading rates (a refreshed cache ignored as stale or invalid), and a notice when the bundled tables are over 90 days old.

by_category.meaning: One bucket per category, largest first.

rows.meaning: Grouped by provider, model, category and cost_status, as in the dashboard's model table.

list_input_rate.meaning: The pricing table's list price, dollars per million input tokens. Says which model is the expensive one; it is not what anything cost. null for a free model or one the table cannot price.

other.meaning: Everything not in rows, so rows + other = totals. null when nothing was folded.
Sessions not listed, plus requests that carry no session id.

by_day.meaning: Local calendar days that have usage, most recent first, at most 31.

undated_requests.meaning: Requests with no timestamp; in totals, in no day.

burn.meaning: The trailing hour, from all usage regardless of range.

cost_per_hour.meaning: null with fewer than 5 requests or no priced spend: too thin to project from.

cost_is_floor.meaning: Some requests in the window have no price.

quota_only.meaning: The window holds only plan-billed work, so there is no dollar rate.

budgets.meaning: Every configured budget, OK ones included. Empty when none is configured.

limits.meaning: Subscription rate-limit windows. Not narrowed by range.

limit_problems.meaning: Limit sources that exist and could not be fully read.

routing.meaning: Recorded routing events in range. Empty unless a hook or --record-routing feeds the journal.

aggregates.meaning: Grouped by agent, model and provider.

withheld.meaning: Test runs in range that a harness saw and recorded nothing for. Counted by UTC day, so a range boundary is a day's, not a second's.

--json.meaning: One object per request. Large: about 130 tokens a row, megabytes on a busy machine. Narrow it with --project, --session, --model, --provider and a range before reading it, or use --csv - for a quarter of the size.

source.meaning: Every source's status joined into one line.

range.meaning: TODAY, 7 DAYS, 30 DAYS, N DAYS or ALL TIME.

billing.meaning: How the request was paid for.

incomplete.meaning: true when the source record lacked a token count it always carries (a format change upstream). The zero beside it is then not recorded, not zero, and the row is never priced.

cost.meaning: Dollars; null when unknown or plan-billed.

api_equivalent_cost.meaning: List-rate value of a plan-billed request. Never charged.

created.meaning: Unix seconds; 0 when the source recorded none.

--routing-json.meaning: Recorded routing events, aggregated. All history unless a range flag is given.

aggregates.meaning: Grouped by agent, model and provider.

withheld.meaning: Test runs a harness saw and recorded nothing for.

--check-budgets.meaning: Budgets past a threshold. Exits 1 when any is; 2 means the check itself failed and printed no document. For headroom on budgets still OK, read budgets in --summary-json.

alerts.meaning: Only budgets at WARN or above.
